content.content:
A ref-path entry takes the accent focus outline while it has the focus. When the focus is on a path entry in the Content section, that entry is marked by an outline drawn in the accent colour role, so a reader can see which entry the focus rests on, and which one the next activation would take, without moving the focus or trying an entry to find out. The outline is the whole of the mark: the entry's text stays the path the block already shows (squvoxyr) and nothing is added to the entry — no element, no label, no glyph, no extra text — so the section still reports the paths the node's ref list carries and the entry still says what it said.

The outline is drawn in the accent colour role recorded for the focused and selected element (qqmrtwor): the accent role, at that role's value and through the token that record names, --vscode-focusBorder, taken as the editor's theme defines that role. This decision spends that role as it is recorded and defines no colour of its own — no literal colour value, no second token, no substitute or fallback for the accent where the theme supplies one, and no re-pointing of the recorded token at another role or value. How thick the outline is, how far it sits from the entry and how it is shaped around the entry's box are not fixed here; what is fixed is that the entry is outlined and the recorded role the outline is drawn in.

The outline is the entry's appearance while the entry holds the focus, and its presence and absence follow that state and no other. It appears as the focus arrives at the entry and stops when the focus leaves it. An entry that does not hold the focus carries no outline from this decision, and nothing here makes the outline a resting decoration of an entry, a mark of the selected node, or a mark that outlives the focus. The pointer is not this state: an entry with the pointer over it and no focus does not take the outline from this decision, and a focused entry keeps it whether or not the pointer is over it. What a path entry looks like on hover is a separate commitment with its own check, and nothing here describes, forbids or implies it. Nothing here says how focus arrives at an entry or where it goes when it leaves; nothing here changes what activating an entry does or how activation is reached; and the focus that draws the outline invokes nothing of its own. The outline is the look of a state the entry can already be in.

The outline belongs to the path entry squvoxyr presents as a visible link in the Content section's block, and to nothing else: not to the block the entry sits in, not to the section or its label, not to the content type shown beside the paths, not to a path mentioned in the selected node's kind, content or rationale text, and not to a path that names no file. It is presentation over that entry as it is recorded, not a re-decision of it: what the entry is, what its text is, where it sits in the section, and what activating it does stay squvoxyr's and rptlovpt's, and the outline neither withholds nor competes with the link presentation the entry is drawn with.

This decision fills exactly the one part squvoxyr left open — what marks a path entry while it has the focus — and leaves every other part of the entry's appearance as it stands. It does not say which colour role the entry's text takes, whether a pointer cursor is shown over the entry, what happens to the entry on hover, which element carries the outline, or which class vocabulary names the entry or its focused state: each of those is a separate commitment with its own check, and none of them is fixed, required, forbidden or implied here. Nor does this decision add any class, style property, stylesheet rule or source of its own: it states the state a path entry is marked in and the recorded role that mark is drawn in, and those are realised where the viewer's styles are written.
content.rationale:
rptlovpt made each path in the Content section's block a control the keyboard can reach, and squvoxyr gave that entry the look that says it can be activated, then stopped: an entry that has been tabbed to is drawn exactly like an entry that has not, so a reader walking the block with the focus cannot tell which of several path entries the next Enter or Space would take, and has to try one to find out. The focus outline is the smallest commitment that closes that gap — no element, no text, no behaviour, only the entry's own appearance carrying the state it is already in — and it is what rptlovpt's focusability was for.

The outline takes the accent role because the panel should mark focus the way the editor around it marks focus, and because a literal value or a second token would put a decision about the viewer's palette inside a decision about a path entry. The recorded row for the focused and selected element is the accent at --vscode-focusBorder (qqmrtwor), so spending that same row — same role, same token, no substitution — keeps the panel's focus mark on the theme's terms and keeps one account of what focus looks like across the panel, without inventing a colour or narrowing the theme to one.

Showing the outline only while the entry holds the focus is what makes it an indicator rather than decoration. An outline that stayed after the focus left would say something false about the state of the block, and one that appeared on hover would either double the hover treatment or replace it; keeping hover out of this decision lets the hover commitment be checked on its own terms as a pointer state, while this one is checked as a focus state. Scoping it to the entry squvoxyr records, rather than to the block or the section, is the same restraint from the other side: marking a region would say the focus is somewhere in it rather than on a particular path, and it would blur the one distinction the entry exists to carry.

Stopping at the state and the role is also what keeps the commitment checkable. Whether a path entry carries an outline while it holds the focus, whether that outline resolves to the recorded role, and whether the outline is gone once the focus leaves are facts a reviewer can point at in the styles and in the running panel: an entry holding focus shown without the accent outline, or an accent outline standing where the focus is not, refutes it without any rule this decision does not state. The remainder — the text colour role, the pointer cursor, the hover rule, the element that draws the outline, its width and shape, the class vocabulary — is still unstated here, and stating any of it would either pre-empt the decision that owns it or restate what that decision says, which is exactly what squvoxyr's own abstentions were there to prevent.
